s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes
salient_findings: Mild aphasia and confusion
Sudden-onset right leg weakness
Mild headache and right facial droop
Extensive white matter changes on MRI
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
key_facts: History of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia
On methotrexate and sulfasalazine treatment
Developed mild aphasia and confusion lasting for several hours
Right leg weakness resolved within 2 days
Presented with mild headache and right facial droop
Neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty
Bilateral upgoing plantars
No motor or sensory deficits
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
CSF analysis showed 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands
MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface

shortlist.label: multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes, high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and CSF analysis showing 4 oligoclonal bands

shortlist.label: autoimmune encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild aphasia and confusion, right leg weakness, and right facial droop, with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level, and CSF analysis showing 12/µL white blood cell count

shortlist.label: stroke
shortlist.why_kept: History of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and episodes of mild aphasia and confusion, right leg weakness, and right facial droop

shortlist.label: optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty, and MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface

shortlist.label: encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Mild aphasia and confusion, right leg weakness, and right facial droop, with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level, and CSF analysis showing 12/µL white blood cell count

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of mild aphasia, confusion, and subsequent episodes of neurological deficits, along with the presence of elevated inflammatory markers, high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and CSF analysis showing 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands, supports an autoimmune process. The brain biopsy findings of a thick exudate in the subarachnoid space with lymphocytes, plasma cells, and multinucleated giant cells further support an autoimmune encephalitis diagnosis.

rejected.label: multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: While the patient has white matter changes on MRI, the presence of a high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody and the brain biopsy findings are not typical for multiple sclerosis.

rejected.label: stroke
rejected.why: The patient's episodes of neurological deficits resolved quickly, which is not typical for a stroke, and the MRI did not show any acute infarct.

rejected.label: optic neuritis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings are not limited to the optic nerve, making optic neuritis an unlikely diagnosis.

rejected.label: encephalopathy
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and findings suggest a more specific autoimmune process rather than a non-specific encephalopathy.

rejected.label: stroke
rejected.why: The patient had no motor or sensory deficits and the MRI Brain showed no acute infarct in diffusion-weighted imaging sequence.
